statement: The geometric monodromy group on the 12 singular members, as a general degree-3 plane-curve pencil varies, is the full symmetric group S12.

group.description: Symmetric group S12 in its natural action

source.location: Proposition1.1 and the restriction-to-a-subfamily monodromy-subgroup observation following Lemma2.1; apply via a general plane section of the irreducible discriminant hypersurface
source.version: arXiv:1809.07293v4 (14 November 2020), primary PDF inspected 4 November 2026

scope: Singular members of general degree-3 projective plane-curve pencils over C, with the pencil varying in the full pencil parameter space.

origin.inheritance_basis: Set d=3, D=3(d−1)²=12 in the general discriminant-section argument.

notes:
Explicit geometric deduction, not a pencil example quoted from Kadets. Let N=d(d+3)/2 be the coefficient-space dimension and Δ⊂P^N the singular-curve discriminant. The incidence of a singular point p and a degree-d form singular at p is a projective bundle over P², since three independent linear conditions are imposed on the coefficients for d≥2. It is irreducible, and its image Δ is an irreducible hypersurface with a general one-nodal member. Its reduced degree is D=3(d−1)² (for d=2 the determinant cubic gives D=3). A general plane Λ⊂P^N meets Δ in an integral plane curve of degree D by Bertini. Restrict to pencils represented by lines ℓ⊂Λ. Their singular members are precisely ℓ∩(Δ∩Λ); Kadets Proposition 1.1 gives full S_D monodromy for this subfamily in characteristic zero. A subfamily monodromy is a subgroup of the full pencil monodromy, which already lies in S_D, so the full group is S_D. Counts and the ordinary-node assertion are also documented in the existing pencil Q1 records. Generators below, when present, use abstract solution labels and are standard generators for S_D, not permutations extracted from numerical continuation.

The degree3(d−1)^2 is the classical homogeneous-discriminant formula attributed to Boole (GKZ, Chapter 1 Example 4.15 and Chapter 9 Example 1.6). Brugallé–Mikhalkin give a later floor-diagram verification. For monodromy records, this supplies only the discriminant degree/irreducibility; the separate sectional-monodromy argument supplies the group.

This is a catalogue application of the classical characteristic-zero sectional-monodromy theorem, called folklore in Kadets, Proposition 1.1. Kadets is cited for an explicit proof, not as the originator of that theorem; the stated Bertini reduction identifies the particular enumerative family.
